language.script_notes: Dutch shows a lot of double vowels (aa, ee, oo, uu), frequent z and w, and the 'ij' digraph. Street names end in -straat, -weg, -laan, -plein, -gracht, -dijk or -steeg.

road_furniture.line_paint: All-white markings: white centre lines and white edge lines.
road_furniture.curb_style: Dedicated cycle paths run alongside almost every road, often surfaced in brownish or red asphalt or red brick.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Blue arrow-shaped direction signs with white lettering point to the nearest towns; small green boards give route numbers on larger roads; blue-and-white poles mark spots where cyclists cross the carriageway. Utility poles are scarce. PostNL branding is common.

architecture.roof_style: Steeply pitched gables on traditional brick houses, often with a hoisting beam projecting near the roof peak; flat roofs on modern blocks and warehouses.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick facades dominate; flat aluminium-clad warehouses stand near waterways.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Narrow canal houses with hoisting beams, windmills, and warehouses along canals.

nature.vegetation: Grassy pastures and farmland split by drainage ditches, with tree-lined canals.
nature.terrain: Extremely flat with no mountains; roughly a quarter of the land lies below sea level, cut by canals, dykes and drained polders. The highest ground is a low hill in the far south-east.

vehicles.plate_color: Yellow with black text on both front and rear, with a blue EU strip on the left carrying 'NL'.
vehicles.plate_format: Letters and digits grouped by hyphens (e.g. 'AB-123-C'); the pattern encodes issue date, not region.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Bicycles are everywhere, sharing cycle paths with mopeds.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Gen 2, 3 and 4, captured from white camera cars.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat northern half, the same language in the north, brick houses
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Yellow plates here versus red-on-white plates; very few utility poles here while square, hole-studded concrete poles are common across the border.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Yellow plates with a blue EU strip
confusion_set.tiebreaker: This country is extremely flat and speaks Dutch; the hilly, forested neighbour with French/German/Luxembourgish signs is not.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat farmland, brick houses, cycling infrastructure
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Dutch has 'ij' and double vowels with streets ending -straat or -weg, and plates are yellow; Danish uses æ, ø, å with streets ending -vej or -gade, and plates are white.
